item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Sep 26, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: NAMIWalks Yolo County — Sat Sep 26, 8:30 AM — Woodland Community College
item.description: Hope is on the move. Residents across Yolo County are coming together for the annual NAMIWalks Yolo County, part of the nation’s largest and most vibrant mental health awareness event series. This year’s theme, “Together We Are NAMIWalks,” reflects the strength, connection, and compassion of our community. Every step taken and every dollar raised fuels NAMI’s free programs, advocacy, and support services – making a lasting difference for the 1 in 5 who experience mental health conditions each year. NAMIWalks is more than a walk: it’s a movement. Participants leave inspired, empowered, and reminded that no one is ever alone. Together, we are stronger. Together, we create hope. Together, we are NAMIWalks. item.title: Pilates in The HIVE Pollinator Garden — Sat Sep 26, 10:00 AM — The HIVE Tasting Room and Kitchen
item.description:
Build strength, improve flexibility, and reconnect with your body in this pilates mat class in the pollinator garden. This energizing, full-body workout combines mindful movement, core-focused exercises, and controlled breathing to leave you feeling stronger, balanced, and refreshed. All ages and abilities welcome! After class, each participant receives a refreshing glass of California Pomegranate Honey Hibiscus Cooler or a sparkling mead beverage. Bring your yoga mat, water and wear comfortable clothes. item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Sep 30, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm

item.title: Shields Library Mural Dedication — Fri Oct 2, 1:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
join us in celebrating our new library mural, created by undergraduate students in the Mural Workshop (ART 171/CHI 171) in Spring 2026. Drawing on the Chicanx tradition of muralism, the students' creative process centered on community engagement, collective storytelling, and sense of place. Vibrant imagery of students, photos from the library's University Archives, and an oak tree bearing the words “Saber es Poder” (“Knowledge is Power”) are among the elements that explore the library as a space where preservation and empowerment meet. Learn more about the mural.
Meet some of the artists who created the mural and see footage of the making of this beautiful work of art. Light refreshments available while they last. Free and open to all.
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Oct 14, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.description:
Iama Embodied Community 🌀 **Move with intention. Connect with your body. Celebrate community.**

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 17, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

item.title: Hope Café — Fri Sep 25, 6:30 PM — International House (I-House)
item.description:
Come celebrate the end of summer and the start of fall with an evening designed to build connection and community. Hope Café is a little bit workshop, a little bit party — a warm, welcoming space where live music, creative activities, and guided conversations invite you to pause, reconnect, and feel like you belong. All you need to do is show up with a curious mind and an open heart. What to Expect: Doors open at 6:30 PM with live world jazz by Nick Carvajal and Jim Frink. Local vendors Jumi Shrub, Enamora Empanadas, and Upper Crust Baking will have snacks and drinks available. Community story sharing and playful creative exercises continue through 8:30 PM, after which guests are encouraged to linger and connect. Sliding Scale: $15-$25
Source: The Dirt

item.description: Join Tyler for an amazing evening of connection that will encourage your heart and remind you that Hope really does change everything HOPE: This Changes Everything Tour An Evening with Tyler Merritt What if hope isn’t something you wait for… but something you choose? Join bestselling author, actor, activist, and beloved storyteller Tyler Merritt for a one-of-a-kind live experience filled with unforgettable stories, humor, music, heartfelt conversation, and practical encouragement. With his signature authenticity, Tyler invites audiences to rediscover what connects us, challenges us, and ultimately gives us reason to hope. item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Fri Sep 25, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt
